description: With `references` (and no recipe) it takes a brand page’s or a pin’s style onto the design, keeping its layout, words and photos. Restyles a design in ONE change with a named art direction: a recipe of faces, three inks, type rules, one layout rule and effects, from documented best practice (describe_catalogue recipes says what each looks like). Words, photos and layout stay, kept readable by the critic. Use it for «make it look like a risograph poster», «Swiss style»; the person’s own name for a style works («газетний стиль»). Live in the open editor, else a new version; a look among its effects needs the design open. Example: { design, recipe: «swiss-grid» }.

artboard.description: one artboard’s id (describe_design / get_design); none: every artboard

design.description: the design’s id or Paletoo link

recipe.description: a recipe id (risograph-poster, swiss-grid, y2k-chrome, editorial-serif, hand-made-zine, neon-night, paper-cut, clay-3d, brutalist, bauhaus, art-deco, retro-70s, minimal-luxury, pop-art, vaporwave, grunge-90s, botanical, tech-startup, broadsheet, constructivist, cyberpunk, soft-pastel, scandi-minimal, film-noir, blueprint, romantic-script, arcade-8bit) or its name in the person’s words; e.g. «swiss-grid»

references.description: Optional visual references, 1–3 public https addresses, best first: the brand’s own page (its type, palette, buttons), then a pin, Behance or Dribbble shot — best the picture’s own address (i.pinimg.com…) — whose layout and look are followed closely; words, photos and logos stay the person’s own.

name: apply_style_recipe
title: Apply a style recipe
